entities.summary:
Agostino III Cusani (c. 1670–1730) was an Italian Catholic bishop from the prominent Milanese Cusani family, which produced multiple generations of Catholic churchmen throughout the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Cusani were a noble Milanese family whose members systematically pursued careers in both civil administration and the Church, and the 'III' designation indicates that this Agostino was the third member of the family to bear the name in an ecclesiastical context.

The Cusani family's repeated appearance in the Catholic hierarchy illustrates the importance of aristocratic family networks in the early modern Church. Noble families from Milan, Venice, and Rome used ecclesiastical appointments as instruments of family advancement and political influence, placing sons in positions that ranged from parish curia to the College of Cardinals. Multiple generations of the same name in religious office was a deliberate strategy of family identity preservation.

Agostino III Cusani's episcopal service contributed to the family tradition of Church administration while placing him within the complex world of eighteenth-century Italian Catholic governance, where family connections, regional loyalties, and individual competence interacted to determine careers and influence.
